body: The NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods page "7.2.5. Does the defect density meet requirements?" says: "Testing defect densities is based on the Poisson distribution The number of defects observed in an area of size \(A\) A --> units is often assumed to have a Poisson distribution with parameter \(A \times D\), A x D , --> where \(D\) D --> is the actual process defect density (\(D\) D --> is defects per unit area). In other words: $$ P(\mbox{Number of Defects } = n) = \frac{(AD)^n}{n!} e^{-AD} \, . $$ --> The questions of primary interest for quality control are: Is the defect density within prescribed limits? Is the defect density less than a prescribed limit? Is the defect density greater than a prescribed limit? Normal approximation to the Poisson We assume that \(AD\) AD --> is large enough so that the normal approximation to the Poisson applies (in other words, \(AD >\) 10 AD > 10 --> for a reasonable…" This card records that page. It does not add a data set the page did not print.
